html:
English and Irish Catholic settlers, sent over from St Kitts under the governor Thomas Warner, began settling Montserrat in 1632. More Irish came later, some as indentured servants.

The island became a sugar colony worked by enslaved Africans brought in the Atlantic slave trade. Irish surnames and place names spread among the whole population.

Montserrat is still called the Emerald Isle of the Caribbean. St Patrick's Day is a public holiday there; it also marks a planned rising by enslaved people on 17 March 1768. The island stayed under the British crown and is a British overseas territory today.
